name: ComfyUI (ROCm)
purpose: ComfyUI workflow editor with ComfyUI-Manager, on the same exclusive Radeon GPU as the llama.cpp and Ollama deployments. Runs from a persistent Python environment in the workspace (<workspace>/venv, seeded once from the image's /opt/venv) so packages that Manager installs for custom nodes survive restarts; torch is pinned by a pip constraint. Custom nodes load from <workspace>/custom_nodes. No ComfyUI authentication: anyone who can reach the port can run workflows and, through Manager (security_level normal), install custom nodes from the default registry.

containers.name: web
command: import runpy, signal, sys; path = sys.argv.pop(1); sys.argv[0] = path; sys.path.insert(0, path.rsplit('/', 1)[0]); signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.default_int_handler); runpy.run_path(path, run_name='__main__')

devices.description: Radeon compute render node, not the display device.
AMD kernel compute device required by ROCm/HIP.

identities.name: /dev/dri/renderD128 image slot
identities.description: Image slot of the GPU: excludes the llama.cpp servers (which hold both slots) but not Ollama (LLM slot only). ComfyUI and Ollama take turns on VRAM: ComfyUI offloads models to RAM after each job and the chat model preset unloads after each reply.

consumers: Browsers and Open WebUI (ComfyUI image connection). No authentication: anyone who can reach the address can run workflows and, through Manager, install registry custom nodes.
